module uart_tx (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    input wire send,
    output reg tx,
    output reg busy
);
    reg [3:0] state;
    reg [2:0] bit_count;
    reg [9:0] shift_reg;

    localparam IDLE = 4'b0000,
               START = 4'b0001,
               DATA = 4'b0010,
               STOP = 4'b0011;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            busy <= 0;
            bit_count <= 0;
            tx <= 1; // Idle state of UART is high
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (send) begin
                        shift_reg <= {1'b1, data_in, 1'b0}; // Stop bit, data, start bit
                        bit_count <= 0;
                        busy <= 1;
                        state <= START;
                    end
                end
                START: begin
                    tx <= 0; // Start bit
                    state <= DATA;
                end
                DATA: begin
                    tx <= shift_reg[bit_count + 1]; // Transmit bit
                    bit_count <= bit_count + 1;
                    if (bit_count == 7) begin
                        state <= STOP; // Move to stop after 8 data bits
                    end
                end
                STOP: begin
                    tx <= 1; // Stop bit
                    busy <= 0;
                    state <= IDLE; // Return to idle
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

It must also have a clock input, an enable signal, and a reset signal.
code:
module spi_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire enable,
    input wire mosi,
    output wire miso,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    input wire [7:0] data_in
);
    
    reg [2:0] state;
    reg [2:0] bit_count;
    reg [7:0] shift_reg;

    localparam IDLE = 3'b000,
               RECEIVE = 3'b001,
               TRANSMIT = 3'b010;

    assign miso = shift_reg[7];

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            bit_count <= 3'b000;
            data_out <= 8'b0;
            shift_reg <= 8'b0;
        end else if (enable) begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (enable) begin
                        shift_reg <= data_in;  // Load data for transmission
                        state <= TRANSMIT;
                        bit_count <= 3'b000;  // Reset bit counter
                    end

                TRANSMIT: begin
                    if (bit_count < 8) begin
                        shift_reg <= {shift_reg[6:0], mosi};  // Shift in MOSI data
                        data_out <= {data_out[6:0], miso};    // Shift out MISO data

                    end else begin
                        state <= IDLE;  // Return to IDLE state after transmission
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

module MemoryAllocator #(parameter MEM_SIZE = 64) (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [2:0] command, // 0: malloc, 1: free, 2: status
    input [5:0] addr,     // address to allocate/free
    output reg [7:0] mem_status // status of memory allocation
);

    reg [MEM_SIZE-1:0] alloc_map;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            alloc_map <= 0;
            mem_status <= 8'b0;
        end else begin
            case (command)
                3'b000: // malloc
                    if (alloc_map[addr] == 1'b0) begin
                        alloc_map[addr] <= 1'b1;
                        mem_status <= 8'b1; // allocated
                    end else begin
                        mem_status <= 8'b0; // already allocated
                    end
                3'b001: // free
                    if (alloc_map[addr] == 1'b1) begin
                        alloc_map[addr] <= 1'b0;
                        mem_status <= 8'b1; // freed
                    end else begin
                        mem_status <= 8'b0; // already freed
                    end
                3'b010: // status
                    mem_status <= alloc_map; // return current status
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

);

        if (rst) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            recovered_clk <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (input_signal) begin
                        state <= RISING_EDGE;
                    end
                end
                RISING_EDGE: begin
                    if (input_signal) begin
                        recovered_clk <= ~recovered_clk; // Toggle clock

                    end else begin
                        state <= IDLE;

            endcase
        end
    end

The input signal `start` transitions the FSM to the `Mapping` state. The FSM remains in `Mapping` for a fixed number of clock cycles, after which it transitions to the `Localizing` state. If the `localize_done` signal is asserted, the FSM goes back to the `Idle` state.
code:
module slam_fsm (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire start,
    input wire localize_done,
    output reg [1:0] state // 00: Idle, 01: Mapping, 10: Localizing
);

    parameter IDLE = 2'b00, MAPPING = 2'b01, LOCALIZING = 2'b10;
    reg [3:0] count; // Counter for mapping duration

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            count <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        state <= MAPPING;
                        count <= 0;
                    end
                end
                MAPPING: begin
                    count <= count + 1;
                    if (count == 4'd5) begin // Stay in mapping state for 5 clock cycles
                        state <= LOCALIZING;
                    end
                end
                LOCALIZING: begin
                    if (localize_done) begin
                        state <= IDLE;
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end

endmodule

module round_robin_arbiter (

    input wire rst,
    input wire [3:0] req,
    output reg [3:0] grant
);

reg [1:0] last_granted;

always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
    if (rst) begin
        grant <= 4'b0000;
        last_granted <= 2'b00;
    end else begin
        case (last_granted)
            2'b00: if (req[0]) begin grant <= 4'b0001; last_granted <= 2'b00; end
                    else if (req[1]) begin grant <= 4'b0010; last_granted <= 2'b01; end
                    else if (req[2]) begin grant <= 4'b0100; last_granted <= 2'b10; end
                    else if (req[3]) begin grant <= 4'b1000; last_granted <= 2'b11; end
                    else grant <= 4'b0000;
            2'b01: if (req[1]) begin grant <= 4'b0010; last_granted <= 2'b01; end
                    else if (req[2]) begin grant <= 4'b0100; last_granted <= 2'b10; end
                    else if (req[3]) begin grant <= 4'b1000; last_granted <= 2'b11; end
                    else if (req[0]) begin grant <= 4'b0001; last_granted <= 2'b00; end
                    else grant <= 4'b0000;
            2'b10: if (req[2]) begin grant <= 4'b0100; last_granted <= 2'b10; end
                    else if (req[3]) begin grant <= 4'b1000; last_granted <= 2'b11; end
                    else if (req[0]) begin grant <= 4'b0001; last_granted <= 2'b00; end
                    else if (req[1]) begin grant <= 4'b0010; last_granted <= 2'b01; end
                    else grant <= 4'b0000;
            2'b11: if (req[3]) begin grant <= 4'b1000; last_granted <= 2'b11; end
                    else if (req[0]) begin grant <= 4'b0001; last_granted <= 2'b00; end
                    else if (req[1]) begin grant <= 4'b0010; last_granted <= 2'b01; end
                    else if (req[2]) begin grant <= 4'b0100; last_granted <= 2'b10; end
                    else grant <= 4'b0000;
            default: grant <= 4'b0000;
        endcase
    end
end

endmodule

Design a simple Stop-and-Wait flow control protocol in Verilog. The sender will send a data bit, and the receiver will acknowledge the received data bit. If the acknowledgment is received, the sender will send the next data bit. The sender will wait for an acknowledgment before sending the next data.
code:
module stop_and_wait (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire send_data,
    input wire recv_ack,
    output reg data_out,
    output reg ack_out
);

    reg [1:0] state; // 0: idle, 1: data sent, 2: ack received

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
            ack_out <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // idle
                    if (send_data) begin
                        data_out <= 1;  // send data
                        state <= 1; // move to data sent state
                    end
                end
                1: begin // data sent
                    ack_out <= 0; // clear ack output
                    if (recv_ack) begin
                        ack_out <= 1; // acknowledge received
                        state <= 2; // move to ack received state
                    end
                end
                2: begin // ack received
                    data_out <= 0; // clear data output
                    if (!send_data) begin
                        state <= 0; // back to idle
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

    input wire b,
    input wire clk,
    output reg out
);

module round_robin_arbiter(  
    input clk,  
    input rst,  
    input [3:0] req,  
    output reg [3:0] grant  
);  
    reg [1:0] current; // to keep track of the current grant position  
    reg [3:0] pending; // pending requests  

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin  
        if (rst) begin  
            grant <= 4'b0000;  
            current <= 2'b00;  
        end else begin  
            pending = req & ~grant; // check for active requests  
            if (pending) begin  
                grant <= (1 << current) & pending; // grant the current request  
            end else begin  
                grant <= 4'b0000; // no grant if no pending requests  
            end  

            current <= (current + 1) % 4; // move to the next request  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

code:
module DFlipFlop (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire D,
    output reg Q
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            Q <= 0;
        end else begin
            Q <= D;
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design an 8-bit shift register with an asynchronous reset. The shift register should shift the data to the left on each clock cycle, and the MSB (Most Significant Bit) should be filled with a serial input bit. The reset should clear the register to all zeros.
code:
module shift_register (  
    input clk,  
    input rst,  
    input serial_in,

);  
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin

description: Design a 3-input NOR gate in Verilog. The NOR gate should output high (1) only when all three inputs are low (0).

Design a 16-bit SRAM cell that allows for read and write operations. The SRAM should have a data input (D), an address input (A), a write enable (WE) signal, and an output (Q). When WE is high, the value at D should be written to the cell addressed by A. When WE is low, the value at the cell addressed by A should be presented at output Q.
code:
module sram_cell(  
    input [15:0] D,  
    input [3:0] A,  
    input WE,

);

description:
Design a Verilog module for a Flash memory cell that can store a single bit of data. The memory cell should have the following functionality:
1. A read operation, which outputs the current stored value.
2. A write operation, triggered by a `write_enable` signal, which allows writing a new bit value into the memory cell.
3. The memory cell should maintain its state until a new value is written.
code:
module flash_memory_cell (
    input wire clk,
    input wire write_enable,
    input wire data_in,
    output reg data_out
);

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (write_enable) begin
        data_out <= data_in; // Write new data on positive clock edge when enabled
    end
end

endmodule

description:
Design a simple Ethernet MAC controller that handles incoming frames. The controller should have the following specifications:
- Inputs:
  - `clk`: Clock signal
  - `rst`: Reset signal (active high)
  - `data_in`: 8-bit data input representing the incoming frame
  - `frame_valid`: Signal indicating if the incoming frame is valid
- Outputs:
  - `data_out`: 8-bit data output representing processed data from the frame
  - `frame_ready`: Signal indicating if the frame has been processed and is ready for output

The controller should process incoming frames when `frame_valid` is asserted. On reset, it should clear its internal state. The `data_out` should reflect the incoming data after processing (for simplicity, let’s just implement a simple pass-through logic).
code:
module ethernet_mac_controller (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    input frame_valid,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg frame_ready
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            data_out <= 8'b0;
            frame_ready <= 1'b0;
        end else if (frame_valid) begin
            data_out <= data_in; // Pass-through logic
            frame_ready <= 1'b1; // Signal that the frame is ready
        end else begin
            frame_ready <= 1'b0; // Frame not ready if no valid input
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) in Verilog that generates a frequency output based on an input control voltage. The VCO has an enable signal, an input control voltage, and a clock input. The output frequency should vary with the control voltage input. The design should include a counter to simulate the frequency output.

Design an 8-channel DMA controller that selects one of the 8 channels based on a 3-bit channel select input. The controller should have an input signal to enable the selected channel and an output signal indicating which channel is currently enabled.
code:
module dma_controller (  
    input wire clk,  
    input wire [2:0] channel_select,  
    input wire enable,  
    output reg [7:0] channel_output  
);  
  
    always @(posedge clk) begin  
        if (enable) begin  
            channel_output <= (1 << channel_select);  
        end else begin  
            channel_output <= 8'b00000000;  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

description: Design a D-latch in Verilog that has the following functionality: when the enable signal (en) is high, the output (q) follows the input (d). When the enable signal is low, the output (q) holds its last value. The D-latch should include a complementary output (q_n) which is the negation of q.

Design a state-space controller in Verilog that takes in a 4-bit input representing the state and produces a 4-bit output representing the control action. The controller should have a clock input and a reset input. The state transition should follow the following logic:
- From state 0000, if input is 0, remain in 0000; if input is 1, transition to state 0001.
- From state 0001, if input is 0, transition to state 0000; if input is 1, transition to state 0010.
- From state 0010, if input is 0, transition to state 0001; if input is 1, transition to state 0011.
- From state 0011, if input is 0, transition to state 0010; if input is 1, transition to state 0000.
The output should equal the current state.

Design a SR-latch using D flip-flops. The latch should set (S=1, R=0) and reset (S=0, R=1) based on the inputs. If both S and R are 0, the latch should maintain its state. If both S and R are 1, the output should be undefined (this should not occur in the simulation). Create an enable input that allows the latch to only change state when enabled.

Design a digital phase shifter that can shift the input phase by 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees based on a 2-bit control signal. The output should be a delayed version of the input signal that represents the phase shift. Use a clock signal to synchronize the output.
code:
module phase_shifter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire din,
    input wire [1:0] phase_select,
    output reg dout
);
    reg [1:0] state;
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            dout <= 0;
            state <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (phase_select)
                2'b00: dout <= din;         // 0 degree phase shift
                2'b01: dout <= din;         // 90 degree phase shift, delayed by one clock cycle
                2'b10: dout <= {din, 1'b0}; // 180 degree phase shift, delayed by two clock cycles
                2'b11: dout <= {1'b0, din}; // 270 degree phase shift, delayed by three clock cycles
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple Turbo Encoder that takes a 1-bit input and produces a 2-bit output based on a simple convolutional encoding scheme. The Turbo Encoder will have a shift register to store the input bits and will produce the output based on the current input and the stored bits.

Design a 24-bit digital-to-analog converter (DAC) that takes a 24-bit input and outputs a corresponding 8-bit output representing the most significant bits of the 24-bit input (i.e., the upper 8 bits). The output should be valid when the input is stable.

Design a temperature sensor data processing circuit that takes a 4-bit binary input representing temperature in degrees Celsius (0 to 15). The circuit should output a 3-bit binary value representing the following conditions:
- If the temperature is less than 5°C, output "000" (Cold).
- If the temperature is between 5°C and 10°C (inclusive), output "001" (Cool).
- If the temperature is between 11°C and 15°C (inclusive), output "010" (Warm).
- If the temperature is greater than 15°C, output "011" (Hot).
code:
module temperature_sensor (
    input [3:0] temp_in,
    output reg [2:0] temp_out
);

always @(*) begin
    if (temp_in < 4'd5) begin
        temp_out = 3'b000; // Cold
    end else if (temp_in >= 4'd5 && temp_in <= 4'd10) begin
        temp_out = 3'b001; // Cool
    end else if (temp_in >= 4'd11 && temp_in <= 4'd15) begin
        temp_out = 3'b010; // Warm
    end else begin
        temp_out = 3'b011; // Hot
    end
end

endmodule

description: Design an 8-bit DRAM cell that allows for reading and writing operations. The cell should have a single data input (D), a data output (Q), a write enable signal (WE), a read enable signal (RE), and a clock signal (CLK). When WE is high, the input data should be written to the cell on the rising edge of CLK. When RE is high, the current data in the cell should be output to Q on the rising edge of CLK. Ensure that both read and write operations cannot occur simultaneously.
code:
module dram_cell (
    input wire [7:0] D,     // Data input
    input wire WE,          // Write enable
    input wire RE,          // Read enable
    input wire CLK,         // Clock
    output reg [7:0] Q      // Data output
);
    reg [7:0] memory;        // Internal memory storage

    always @(posedge CLK) begin
        if (WE && !RE) begin
            memory <= D;      // Write data to memory
        end
        if (RE && !WE) begin
            Q <= memory;      // Read data from memory
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a watchdog timer in Verilog that resets an output signal if an enable signal is not toggled within a set timeout period. The watchdog timer should take a clock input and reset its timer whenever the enable signal is high. If the timer reaches its timeout period, the output signal should go low, indicating a timeout event.

Design a simplified version of the Data Encryption Standard (DES) encryption algorithm that takes a 64-bit plaintext input and a 64-bit key input. The module will perform a single round of DES, which consists of an initial permutation, a Feistel function, and a final permutation. The output will be a 64-bit ciphertext.

Design a simple RC oscillator that produces a clock signal whose frequency is determined by the RC time constant. The oscillator toggles its output every time a counter reaches a certain value, simulating the behavior of a basic RC circuit.

Design a Carry-Skip Adder (CSA) in Verilog that takes two n-bit binary numbers and a carry input, and produces an n-bit sum and a carry output. The carry-skip adder should have a parameterized width for n (e.g., n = 4). The CSA should skip the carry propagation for groups of bits based on the carry input of the preceding group.

Implement a simple instruction pipeline with stages for Fetch (IF), Decode (ID), Execute (EX), and Write Back (WB). The pipeline should support a 2-stage instruction fetching mechanism where the next instruction is fetched while the current instruction is being decoded.

Design a 4-bit Brent-Kung adder in Verilog. The adder should take two 4-bit inputs and produce a 5-bit output (to accommodate carry). The Brent-Kung adder uses a tree structure to generate carries in a parallel fashion. Implement the carry generation and sum computation correctly.

Design an 8-bit Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) that takes an 8-bit binary input representing an analog signal and outputs a corresponding 4-bit binary value that is a scaled representation of the input. The scaling should be such that the maximum 8-bit input (255) corresponds to the maximum 4-bit output (15).
code:
module adc_8to4 (
    input [7:0] analog_input,
    output reg [3:0] digital_output
);

always @(*) begin
    digital_output = analog_input >> 4; // Scale down by 16
end

endmodule

description: Design a 2-stage pipeline system that takes an 8-bit input, doubles it in stage 1, and adds 5 in stage 2. The output should be a 9-bit value, representing the result after both stages.
Design a 64-bit counter that increments on every positive edge of a clock signal. The counter should reset to zero when a reset signal is asserted. The counter should have a 64-bit output.

Design a Verilog module for a simple linked list traversal. The module should take an input for the head of the linked list and a clock signal. On each clock cycle, it should output the current node's value and move to the next node until it reaches the end of the list (indicated by a null pointer). The linked list nodes can be represented using a simple structure with a data field and a pointer to the next node.

Design a 2-stage pipeline system that takes an input data signal, processes it through two stages, and outputs the final processed data. The first stage should perform a simple arithmetic operation (e.g., addition of a constant), and the second stage should perform another arithmetic operation (e.g., multiplication by a constant).

Design a temperature-based shutdown controller in Verilog. The controller shall monitor a temperature input and trigger a shutdown signal when the temperature exceeds a threshold. The controller must include a reset signal and incorporate delay logic to prevent rapid toggling of the shutdown signal.
Design a 3-input NOR gate in Verilog. The gate should output high only when all three inputs are low. Implement the logic and test it using a testbench that verifies all possible input combinations.

Design a 4-bit shift register with the following specifications:
- The shift register has an input `data_in` of 4 bits and a `shift` control signal.
- On the rising edge of the `clk`, if `shift` is high, the shift register should shift left, and the least significant bit (LSB) should be filled with `0`.
- If `shift` is low, the data in the register should hold its value.
- The output should be a 4-bit signal `data_out` representing the current state of the shift register.
code:
module shift_register(
    input clk,
    input shift,
    input [3:0] data_in,
    output reg [3:0] data_out
);
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (shift) begin
            data_out <= {data_out[2:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left and fill LSB with 0
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Verilog module that implements a simple PNG compression type filter, specifically the "Sub" filter. The "Sub" filter computes the difference between the current pixel and the pixel to the left. Given a pixel data input and a pixel to the left, the module should output the filtered pixel data. The input will be an 8-bit current pixel and an 8-bit pixel to the left. The output should also be an 8-bit filtered pixel.

Design a 1-bit SRAM cell that can store a single bit of data. The SRAM cell has two inputs: `write_enable` and `data_in`, and one output: `data_out`. When `write_enable` is high, the input `data_in` should be written to the SRAM cell. When `write_enable` is low, the output `data_out` should reflect the stored data in the SRAM cell.
code:
module sram_cell (

    input wire data_in,
    output reg data_out
);
    always @(posedge write_enable) begin

endmodule

description: Design a 2-channel DMA controller that transfers data from one source to two different destinations. Each channel can be activated independently with a start signal. The controller should have a clock and reset signal, and it should output a transfer complete signal when the data transfer for either channel is finished.

Design a 32-bit comparator that compares two 32-bit inputs A and B. The comparator should output three signals: A_greater, A_equal, and A_less, which indicate whether A is greater than, equal to, or less than B, respectively.

Design a 1-bit SRAM cell that has inputs for data (D), write enable (WE), and a clock signal (CLK). The SRAM cell should store the value of D when WE is high on a rising edge of CLK and maintain the stored value when WE is low.

Design a fan speed controller that adjusts the speed of a fan based on temperature input. The controller will have the following behavior: If the temperature is below 20 degrees Celsius, the fan speed will be set to 0 (OFF). If the temperature is between 20 and 30 degrees, the fan speed will be set to 1 (LOW). If the temperature is between 30 and 40 degrees, the fan speed will be set to 2 (MEDIUM). If the temperature is above 40 degrees, the fan speed will be set to 3 (HIGH). The design should include a clock signal and a reset signal.
code:
module FanSpeedController(
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [7:0] temperature, // 0 to 255 degrees Celsius
    output reg [1:0] fan_speed // 00: OFF, 01: LOW, 10: MEDIUM, 11: HIGH
);
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            fan_speed <= 2'b00; // OFF
        end else begin
            case (temperature)
                8'b00000000: fan_speed <= 2'b00; // 0 degrees
                8'b00010100: fan_speed <= 2'b01; // 20 degrees
                8'b00111010: fan_speed <= 2'b10; // 30 degrees
                8'b00111011: fan_speed <= 2'b11; // 40 degrees
                8'b11111111: fan_speed <= 2'b11; // 255 degrees
                default: begin
                    if (temperature < 20) begin
                        fan_speed <= 2'b00; // OFF
                    end else if (temperature < 30) begin
                        fan_speed <= 2'b01; // LOW
                    end else if (temperature < 40) begin
                        fan_speed <= 2'b10; // MEDIUM
                    end else begin
                        fan_speed <= 2'b11; // HIGH
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Create a Divide-by-4 circuit that takes a 4-bit binary input and produces a 2-bit output representing the quotient when the input is divided by 4. The output should be valid on every positive edge of a clock signal. The output should also reset to 0 when a reset signal is asserted.
code:
module divide_by_4 (
    input wire [3:0] in,
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    output reg [1:0] out
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            out <= 2'b00;
        end else begin
            out <= in[3:2]; // Divide by 4 by taking the two higher bits
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a combinational circuit that evaluates a polynomial of the form P(x) = a0 + a1*x + a2*x^2 + ... + an*x^n, where the coefficients a0, a1, a2, ..., an are specified as inputs, and x is also an input. The output should be the result of the polynomial evaluation. Assume that the maximum degree of the polynomial is 4 for simplicity.

Design a simple SR-latch using Verilog. The SR-latch should have two inputs, S (Set) and R (Reset), and two outputs, Q and Qn (not Q). The output Q should be set to 1 when S is high and R is low, and reset to 0 when R is high and S is low. When both S and R are low, the output should retain its previous state. When both S and R are high, the state is considered invalid.
Design a 32-bit multiplier that takes two 32-bit inputs and produces a 64-bit output. The output should be the product of the two inputs.

Create a Verilog module that implements a simple Support Vector Machine (SVM) binary classifier. The SVM will take two 8-bit inputs representing the feature vectors of two data points. It will also take a 1-bit input representing the weight (1 for Class 1, 0 for Class 0). The output should be 1 if the inputs are classified as Class 1 and 0 if classified as Class 0. The SVM logic can be simplified to a linear decision boundary: if the dot product of the feature vectors and weights exceeds a certain threshold, classify as Class 1, otherwise Class 0.

Design a Verilog module that implements a simple Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) controller. The controller takes an input signal representing workload (in the range of 0 to 15) and adjusts the output clock frequency and voltage level based on predefined workload thresholds. The output frequency and voltage levels are represented as 2-bit and 3-bit values, respectively. The mapping is as follows:
- Workload 0-3: Frequency 00 (low), Voltage 000 (low)
- Workload 4-7: Frequency 01 (medium), Voltage 001 (medium)
- Workload 8-11: Frequency 10 (high), Voltage 010 (high)
- Workload 12-15: Frequency 11 (max), Voltage 011 (max)
code:
module DVFS_Controller (
    input wire [3:0] workload,
    output reg [1:0] frequency,
    output reg [2:0] voltage
);
    always @(workload) begin
        case (workload)
            4'b0000, 4'b0001, 4'b0010, 4'b0011: begin
                frequency = 2'b00; // low frequency
                voltage = 3'b000; // low voltage
            end
            4'b0100, 4'b0101, 4'b0110, 4'b0111: begin
                frequency = 2'b01; // medium frequency
                voltage = 3'b001; // medium voltage
            end
            4'b1000, 4'b1001, 4'b1010, 4'b1011: begin
                frequency = 2'b10; // high frequency
                voltage = 3'b010; // high voltage
            end
            4'b1100, 4'b1101, 4'b1110, 4'b1111: begin
                frequency = 2'b11; // max frequency
                voltage = 3'b011; // max voltage
            end
            default: begin
                frequency = 2'b00; // default low frequency
                voltage = 3'b000; // default low voltage
            end
        endcase
    end
endmodule

description: Design an 8-bit divider module that divides two 8-bit unsigned integers. The output should be an 8-bit quotient and an 8-bit remainder. Implement the division using a sequential algorithm with states. The module should take a start signal to begin the division process and an input valid signal to indicate when the inputs are ready. It should output the results when the process is complete.

Design a PCIe endpoint controller that manages a simple state machine. The state machine should have three states: IDLE, TRANSFER, and DONE. The controller should transition through these states based on input signals: a start signal to begin transferring, and a done signal to indicate completion of the transfer. The controller should output the current state and a signal indicating when a transfer is in progress.

Design a 2-bit divider that takes a 2-bit binary number as the dividend and a 2-bit binary number as the divisor and outputs a 2-bit quotient and a 2-bit remainder. The divisor should not be zero, and handle division by zero gracefully by setting the quotient and remainder to 0.

Design an 8-bit DRAM cell that can store and retrieve data. The DRAM cell should have the following inputs: a write enable (we), a read enable (re), an 8-bit data input (data_in), and a 3-bit address input (addr). The output should be an 8-bit data output (data_out). When write enable is high, data_in should be written to the cell at the specified address. When read enable is high, the stored data at the specified address should be output on data_out. The data should be stored in a memory array of 8-bit registers.
code:
module dram_cell (  
    input wire we,  
    input wire re,  
    input wire [7:0] data_in,  
    input wire [2:0] addr,  
    output reg [7:0] data_out  
);  
    reg [7:0] memory [0:7];  // 8-bit memory array with 8 entries  
  
    always @(posedge we or posedge re) begin  
        if (we) begin  
            memory[addr] <= data_in;  // Write data to memory  
        end  
        if (re) begin  
            data_out <= memory[addr];  // Read data from memory  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

description:
Design a 2-channel DMA (Direct Memory Access) controller in Verilog. The controller should have the following specifications:

Design a simple linear voltage regulator in Verilog that accepts a 5-bit input representing the desired voltage level (0 to 31), and outputs a 5-bit regulated voltage level. The output should be the same as the input but limited to a maximum of 20 (i.e., if the input is greater than 20, the output should be 20).
Design a 3-input AND gate in Verilog that takes three binary inputs and produces one binary output. The output should be high only when all three inputs are high.

Design a simple Ethernet MAC controller state machine that processes incoming frames. The MAC should have states for IDLE, RECEIVE, and PROCESS. The state machine should transition to the RECEIVE state when a frame is detected and then to the PROCESS state after the frame has been fully received. The system should return to the IDLE state after processing the frame. The inputs to the state machine include a frame_ready signal indicating when a frame has started arriving and a frame_done signal indicating when the frame has been fully received. Design a Verilog module that implements a 4-point Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT). The module should take a 4-bit input vector and produce a 4-bit output vector. The DCT is defined for a 4-point input as follows:

Design a Wallace tree adder in Verilog that takes two 8-bit binary numbers as inputs and computes their sum. The output should be an 8-bit sum and a carry-out bit.

Design a Verilog module that performs LU decomposition on a 2x2 matrix. The module should take a 4-bit binary input representing the elements of the matrix and output the lower and upper triangular matrices. The input format will be as follows: the first two bits represent the first row, and the next two bits represent the second row of the matrix.

Design a 3x3 image convolution module in Verilog that takes an 8-bit pixel value and a 3x3 kernel, applies the convolution operation, and outputs a single 8-bit result. The kernel values can be both positive and negative. The input image data is assumed to be provided as a single 8-bit pixel value, while the kernel is provided in a 3x3 format, flattened into a single 9-bit value (for simplicity).

Design an RC oscillator using a Verilog module that simulates the behavior of an RC circuit to generate a clock signal. The oscillator should toggle its output at a rate determined by a configurable resistor and capacitor value. Use a counter to create a feedback loop that determines the output frequency.
code:
module rc_oscillator (
    input wire clk,       // System clock
    input wire reset,     // Reset signal
    output reg out        // Output clock signal
);
    reg [7:0] counter;    // 8-bit counter for frequency division
    parameter MAX_COUNT = 255; // Adjust this value to change oscillation frequency

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            counter <= 8'b0;
            out <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (counter >= MAX_COUNT) begin
                counter <= 8'b0;
                out <= ~out; // Toggle output
            end else begin
                counter <= counter + 1;
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple watchdog timer in Verilog. The timer should be reset by an input signal every time it is received. If the reset signal is not received within a specified timeout period, the timer should output a 'timeout' signal. The timer should be clocked and function based on a clock input.

Design a PID controller in Verilog that takes a setpoint (SP), a process variable (PV), and outputs a control signal (CV) based on the proportional, integral, and derivative terms. The controller should have adjustable gains for each term and be able to accumulate the integral and calculate the derivative based on the process variable.

Design a simplified DES encryption block that takes a 64-bit input plaintext and a 64-bit key and produces a 64-bit ciphertext. The encryption process should include a key schedule to generate subkeys for each of the 16 rounds and perform a simplified version of the Feistel function. The actual implementation should not detail the entire DES algorithm but rather demonstrate the structure and flow with simplified logic.

Design a reset controller that manages a system reset signal. The controller should have an input `reset_n` (active low reset) and a clock signal `clk`. On the rising edge of `clk`, if `reset_n` is low, the output `reset_out` should be asserted high for 10 clock cycles before returning to low. If `reset_n` is high, `reset_out` should remain low.
code:

module arq_system(
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input data_in,
    input ack,
    output reg data_out
);

    reg [1:0] state; // 2-bit state for state machine
    reg [3:0] counter; // Count cycles without ack
    parameter IDLE = 2'b00, SEND = 2'b01, WAIT_ACK = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            counter <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    data_out <= data_in;
                    state <= SEND;
                    counter <= 0; // Reset counter
                end
                SEND: begin
                    if (ack) begin
                        state <= IDLE; // Acknowledgment received, go back to IDLE
                    end else begin
                        counter <= counter + 1; // Increment counter
                        if (counter == 4'b1111) begin
                            state <= SEND; // Resend the last data bit
                        end else begin
                            state <= WAIT_ACK; // Wait for ack
                        end
                    end
                end
                WAIT_ACK: begin
                    if (ack) begin
                        state <= IDLE; // Acknowledgment received
                    end else begin
                        counter <= counter + 1; // Increment counter
                        if (counter == 4'b1111) begin
                            state <= SEND; // Resend the last data bit

            endcase

- `z2`: measurement from sensor 2 (position)
- `dt`: time delta for the prediction step (fixed value)

The filter will produce an output:
- `x_est`: estimated position of the object

Assume initial estimates and parameters for simplicity.
code:
module kalman_filter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [15:0] z1,
    input wire [15:0] z2,
    input wire [15:0] dt,
    output reg [15:0] x_est
);

    reg [15:0] x_prev;
    reg [15:0] P_prev;
    reg [15:0] Q; // process noise covariance
    reg [15:0] R; // measurement noise covariance
    reg [15:0] K; // Kalman gain

    initial begin
        x_prev = 16'b0; // initial state estimate
        P_prev = 16'b1000; // initial estimation error covariance
        Q = 16'b1; // process noise
        R = 16'b10; // measurement noise
    end

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            x_prev <= 16'b0;
            P_prev <= 16'b1000;
        end else begin
            // Prediction step
            x_est <= x_prev; // prediction
            P_prev <= P_prev + Q; // update the error covariance
            
            // Update step
            K <= P_prev / (P_prev + R); // Kalman gain
            x_prev <= x_est + K * ( (z1 + z2) / 2 - x_est ); // update state estimate
            P_prev <= (1 - K) * P_prev; // update error covariance
        end
    end
endmodule

    input [7:0] B,
    input [2:0] opcode,
    output reg [7:0] R,
    output reg Z
);
    always @(*) begin
        case (opcode)
            3'b000: R = A + B; // Addition
            3'b001: R = A - B; // Subtraction
            3'b010: R = A & B; // AND
            3'b011: R = A | B; // OR
            3'b100: R = A ^ B; // XOR

            3'b111: R = (A < B) ? 8'b00000001 : 8'b00000000; // A < B comparison
            default: R = 8'b00000000; // Default case
        endcase
        Z = (R == 8'b00000000) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0; // Zero flag
    end
endmodule

The module should take a matrix of weights as input and output a matrix of shortest paths. The input matrix will be 4x4 for simplicity, where 'inf' is represented as a large number (e.g., 999) to indicate no direct path between vertices.
code:
module floyd_warshall(
    input [15:0] weights,  // 4x4 matrix flattened (16 bits for 4 weights)
    output reg [15:0] dist // 4x4 matrix of shortest paths flattened
);
    integer i, j, k;
    reg [15:0] temp_dist [0:3][0:3]; // 4x4 distance array

    always @* begin
        // Initialize the distance matrix with weights
        for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
            for (j = 0; j < 4; j = j + 1) begin
                if (i == j) 
                    temp_dist[i][j] = 0; // Distance to self is 0
                else 
                    temp_dist[i][j] = (weights[(i*4 + j)*4 +: 4] == 4'b1111) ? 999 : weights[(i*4 + j)*4 +: 4]; // 'inf' check
            end
        end

        // Floyd-Warshall algorithm
        for (k = 0; k < 4; k = k + 1) begin
            for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                for (j = 0; j < 4; j = j + 1) begin
                    if (temp_dist[i][j] > temp_dist[i][k] + temp_dist[k][j]) begin
                        temp_dist[i][j] = temp_dist[i][k] + temp_dist[k][j];
                    end
                end
            end
        end

        // Flatten the distance array for output
        for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
            for (j = 0; j < 4; j = j + 1) begin
                dist[(i*4 + j)*4 +: 4] = temp_dist[i][j];
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple Automatic Repeat reQuest (ARQ) system in Verilog. The system should include a sender and a receiver. The sender sends a data bit along with an acknowledgment (ACK) signal from the receiver. If the receiver detects an error in the received data, it will send a negative acknowledgment (NACK) signal back to the sender. The sender should then resend the last data bit until it receives an ACK signal. Assume that there is a simple error detection mechanism that flips a bit with a 10% probability.

module arq_system(
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input data_in,
    output reg data_out,
    output reg ack,
    output reg nack
);
    reg [1:0] state; // 0: idle, 1: sending, 2: wait_ack, 3: error
    reg error_detected;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
            ack <= 0;
            nack <= 0;
            error_detected <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // idle
                    data_out <= data_in;
                    ack <= 0;
                    nack <= 0;
                    state <= 1;
                end
                1: begin // sending
                    // Simulate random error detection
                    error_detected <= ($random % 10 == 0); // 10% chance of error
                    if (error_detected) begin
                        state <= 3; // go to error state
                    end else begin
                        ack <= 1; // simulate successful send
                        state <= 2; // wait for ack
                    end
                end
                2: begin // wait for ack
                    if (ack) begin
                        state <= 0; // go back to idle
                    end
                end
                3: begin // error detected
                    nack <= 1; // send nack
                    state <= 0; // go back to idle
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule
